q: The charge of a stores depot is transferred from one stockholder to another. A deficiency in stock is brought out in the verification carried out at the time of the transfer. Responsibility for the deficiency rests:

options.A: Automatically on the incoming stockholder, from the date he signs the charge report
options.B: Primarily on the outgoing stockholder in whose custody the deficiency occurred, the incoming stockholder taking over only the balances verified and accepted by him
options.C: On the stock verifier who carried out the verification
options.D: On the supplier who last supplied the item

e: On transfer of charge, the outgoing stockholder is primarily liable for a deficiency occurring in his custody; the incoming stockholder takes over only balances actually verified and accepted by him on the charge report.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The fall clause protects the Railway against a fall in the price at which the contractor sells the same item to another buyer during the currency of the contract.
2. The price variation clause adjusts the contract price with reference to the movement of the indices and formula stipulated in the contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The fall clause protects the Railway if the contractor sells the same item cheaper to another buyer, and the price variation clause adjusts price by the stipulated indices and formula; both statements correctly describe the clauses.

q: The option clause in a stores contract is distinguished from a 'repeat order' in that:

options.A: The option clause is exercised after the contract has expired, while a repeat order is placed during its currency
options.B: Both are exercised only after inviting fresh tenders
options.C: A repeat order is placed free of cost, while the option quantity is paid for
options.D: The option clause is exercised during the currency of the same contract on its own terms, while a repeat order is a fresh order placed on the basis of a previous order

e: The option clause is exercised during the currency of the same contract on its own terms, while a repeat order is a fresh, separate order placed later on the basis of a previous order and its rates.

q: A stores item is of a specialised nature and is manufactured by only a few approved sources. Procurement of such an item is appropriately made through:

options.A: An open tender in all cases, however specialised the item may be
options.B: A limited tender invited from the approved/registered firms dealing in the item
options.C: An e-auction among the approved sources
options.D: A cash purchase from the open market by the storekeeper

e: A specialised item made by only a few approved sources is procured by limited tender from approved or registered firms for that item; open tender to all firms would not yield capable suppliers.

q: A stores contract is placed on firm and fixed price terms, with no price variation clause. During the currency of the contract, market prices rise and the supplier claims payment at a higher rate. The claim is:

options.A: Not admissible, the supplier being bound to supply at the contracted firm price
options.B: Admissible to the extent of the rise in the market rate
options.C: Admissible if the depot officer certifies the rise in prices
options.D: Admissible after approval of the stock verifier

e: Under a firm and fixed price contract with no price variation clause, the supplier is bound to supply at the contracted price; a later market rise does not make a higher rate claim admissible.

q: Tools and plant issued to a field official for use on works are lost while in his custody and the loss is established after enquiry. Until the loss is regularised, the items:

options.A: Stand automatically removed from all records on the date of the loss
options.B: Are treated as consumed on the work without any enquiry
options.C: Continue to be borne on the Tools and Plant register as outstanding against the official, the cost being recovered from the person responsible or written off under competent sanction
options.D: Are replaced free of cost by the supplier

e: Tools and plant lost in a field official custody remain borne on the Tools and Plant register as outstanding against him until the loss is enquired into and the cost is recovered or written off under competent sanction.

q: Consumption of a vital stores item rises sharply during the lead time of a replenishment order, yet the depot is able to meet all demands without a stock-out. This is possible mainly because of the:

options.A: Dead surplus held in the depot
options.B: Earnest money held from tenderers
options.C: Scrap awaiting disposal in the depot
options.D: Safety (buffer) stock provided for the item over and above the normal lead-time consumption

e: Safety or buffer stock is held over and above normal lead-time consumption to absorb surges in consumption or delay in replenishment, which is why demands were met without stock-out despite the sharp rise.

q: A depot orders an item in very large quantities at long intervals in order to save ordering cost, but finds that the cost of holding the large stock is mounting heavily. The Economic Order Quantity approach resolves this by fixing the order quantity at which:

options.A: Only the ordering cost is the minimum, regardless of the holding cost
options.B: The sum of the ordering cost and the inventory carrying (holding) cost is the minimum
options.C: The purchase price per unit is the maximum
options.D: No safety stock is required to be held

e: Economic Order Quantity balances ordering cost against carrying cost; the optimum quantity is where the sum of annual ordering cost and annual inventory holding cost is minimum.

q: Two stores items bear Price Ledger (PL) numbers beginning with the same first two digits. This indicates that the items:

options.A: Belong to the same major group of allied stores in the codification system
options.B: Were purchased from the same supplier
options.C: Have the same book rate per unit
options.D: Are both classified as dead surplus

e: In the PL codification the first two digits denote the major group of allied stores; items sharing them belong to the same group, regardless of supplier, rate or surplus status.

q: A zonal railway inducts a new series of coaches, and the consumption of the associated maintenance stores rises substantially above the past trend. At the periodical review, the Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of the affected items is:

options.A: Kept unchanged, as AAC once fixed can never be revised
options.B: Reduced to the lowest past consumption
options.C: Revised upward to reflect the changed pattern of consumption, so that adequate coverage is provided
options.D: Fixed only by the Railway Board in every such case

e: Average Annual Consumption is reviewed periodically and revised to reflect changed consumption patterns, such as induction of a new coach series; keeping an outdated AAC would leave coverage inadequate.

q: Finance, while vetting an indent for a non-stock item, finds that an equivalent item is already stocked in the depot and is available for issue. The proper course on vetting is to:

options.A: Pass the indent without any remark, vetting being a mere formality
options.B: Advise the supplier to be selected for the purchase
options.C: Carry out the physical verification of the depot stock itself
options.D: Point out the availability of the stocked item and question the propriety of the fresh procurement, so that duplicate purchase is avoided

e: On vetting a non-stock indent, Finance must point out that an equivalent stocked item is available and question the propriety of fresh purchase, preventing duplicate procurement and wasteful expenditure.

q: An inspection note is distinguished from a receipt note in stores procedure in that:

options.A: Both documents are prepared by the supplier of the material
options.B: The inspection note records the result of inspection of the material by the inspecting authority, while the receipt note is prepared by the consignee depot for material received, inspected and accepted into stock
options.C: The receipt note is prepared before the material is despatched by the supplier
options.D: The inspection note is used for issuing stores to consuming departments

e: The inspection note is the inspecting authority record of the result of inspection, while the receipt note is prepared by the consignee depot for material received, inspected and accepted into stock; they are distinct documents.

q: A credit has remained outstanding under Sales Suspense for a long time. On review, it is traced to a scrap lot whose delivery to the purchaser was completed long ago, but whose final adjustment was omitted. The balance is cleared by:

options.A: Transferring the amount to the final head of account to which the sale value is creditable, since the delivery stands completed
options.B: Refunding the amount to the purchaser without any enquiry
options.C: Debiting the amount to Purchase Suspense
options.D: Writing off the amount as a loss of stores

e: A long-outstanding Sales Suspense credit for a lot already delivered is cleared by transfer to the final head creditable for the sale value; refund or write-off would be wrong when delivery stands completed.

q: An item is slow-moving in one depot, but the periodical surplus statement shows that another depot of the same railway consumes the item regularly. The correct disposal of the item is by:

options.A: Immediate sale as scrap through e-auction
options.B: Surveying it off as dead surplus without further enquiry
options.C: Transferring it to the depot which requires it, in preference to its disposal outside the Railway
options.D: Returning it to the original supplier for a refund

e: Surplus at one depot that is regularly consumed at another depot of the same railway is transferred to the needing depot in preference to outside disposal, optimising use of existing stock.

q: A lot of scrap has been sold in an e-auction and the sale order issued, but the purchaser has not yet taken delivery of the material. Until delivery is effected, the material:

options.A: Becomes the property of the stock verifier
options.B: May be issued by the depot to any consuming department
options.C: Is removed from the depot premises by the depot staff themselves
options.D: Remains in the custody of the depot, segregated as sold material, and is delivered only to the purchaser against the delivery order

e: Sold scrap pending delivery remains in depot custody, segregated as sold material, and is delivered only to the purchaser against the delivery order; it cannot be re-issued to departments.

q: Stores consigned to a depot are found damaged on receipt, the damage being attributable to transit. Before the material is accepted into priced stock, the depot is required to:

options.A: Accept the material silently and bear the loss in the depot accounts
options.B: Record the damage, lodge a claim on the carrier/supplier as admissible under the terms of supply, and deal with the material as per the settlement of the claim
options.C: Sell the damaged material to the carrier in an e-auction
options.D: Debit the value of the damage to the Stock Adjustment Account without any claim

e: For transit-damaged stores the depot must record the damage and lodge a claim on the carrier or supplier as admissible under the supply terms before accepting the material into priced stock, dealing with it as per claim settlement.

q: During stock verification, certain stores are found in a damaged and unserviceable condition, though the quantities tally with the book balance. Such stores are dealt with by:

options.A: Recording them as a shortage on a stock sheet
options.B: Treating them as excess stock of the depot
options.C: Segregating them and bringing them before the Survey Committee for condemnation, quantity shortage being not involved
options.D: Issuing them to departments as serviceable stores

e: Damaged and unserviceable stores whose quantities tally are not a shortage; they are segregated and placed before the Survey Committee for condemnation and disposal, since the difference is of condition, not quantity.

q: On agreement of a depot's records, the quantities in the bin (custody) accounts tally with the priced stores ledger, but the value of stock in hand differs after a revision of the book rate of an item. The value difference is rectified:

options.A: Through the Stock Adjustment Account, by adjusting the difference in the value of the stock in hand consequent on the rate revision
options.B: By altering the quantities recorded in the bin cards
options.C: By recovering the difference from the stockholder in cash
options.D: By debiting the difference to Purchase Suspense

e: A value difference arising solely from revision of book rate, quantities being correct, is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account for the stock in hand; bin card quantities are not altered.

q: Stores are issued from a depot for a capital work sanctioned under a Plan Head. Before the issue is posted, the Stores Accounts office must ensure that the issue note bears:

options.A: The revenue Primary Unit applicable to ordinary repairs in all cases
options.B: No allocation, as issues for works require no head of account
options.C: Only the name of the contractor executing the work
options.D: The capital head of account (Plan Head and work) to which the cost of the stores is debitable

e: Issues for a capital work must bear the capital head of account - Plan Head and specific work - to which the stores cost is debitable; a revenue Primary Unit for ordinary repairs would misclassify the charge.

q: At any point of time during the year, a stores depot can state its exact stock position of an item without a special physical count. This is possible because railway stores accounts follow the:

options.A: Periodic inventory system, in which stock is ascertained only at the year end
options.B: Perpetual inventory system, in which receipts and issues are recorded continuously in the custody and priced accounts
options.C: System of accounting stores only on their final consumption
options.D: System of valuing stores only at the time of stock verification

e: Railways follow the perpetual inventory system: every receipt and issue is recorded continuously in custody bin cards and the priced ledger, so the exact stock position is known at any time without a special count.

q: Against an open tender for stores, only one valid offer is received, and the rate quoted is found reasonable with reference to the last accepted rate and the market rate. The tender:

options.A: Must be rejected in all cases, a single offer being never acceptable
options.B: Is accepted automatically without examination by the Tender Committee
options.C: May be considered and accepted by the competent authority on the recommendations of the Tender Committee, with the reasons for accepting a single offer recorded
options.D: Can be accepted only by the Railway Board

e: A single valid offer is not automatically invalid; if the rate is reasonable against last accepted and market rates, the Tender Committee may recommend and the competent authority may accept it with reasons recorded.

q: A supplier persistently defaults in supplying stores, and the competent authority terminates the contract. The Railway may thereafter:

options.A: Procure the stores by risk purchase at the risk and cost of the defaulting supplier, besides taking action regarding the security deposit as per the contract conditions
options.B: Only wait indefinitely for the supplier to resume supplies
options.C: Recover the loss from the depot stockholder
options.D: Cancel all other contracts of other suppliers for the same item

e: On termination for persistent default, the Railway may make risk purchase at the risk and cost of the defaulting supplier and deal with his security deposit as per contract conditions, besides other contractual remedies.

q: Stores are found defective after the expiry of the warranty period stipulated in the contract, the defect not having been noticed or claimed within that period. The cost of repair or replacement of the stores:

options.A: Must still be borne by the supplier under the warranty clause
options.B: Is recovered from the earnest money of the supplier
options.C: Is adjusted through the Sales Suspense Account
options.D: Cannot ordinarily be claimed from the supplier under the warranty clause, and is borne by the Railway

e: Warranty covers defects noticed and claimed within the warranty period; a defect found after expiry, not claimed in time, cannot ordinarily be claimed from the supplier and its cost is borne by the Railway.

q: A risk purchase is made against a defaulting supplier at a rate lower than the rate in the original contract. The amount recoverable from the defaulting supplier on account of extra cost of the risk purchase is:

options.A: The entire value of the risk purchase
options.B: Nil on that account, there being no excess cost over the original contract price
options.C: Twice the difference between the two rates
options.D: The earnest money deposited by all the tenderers

e: Risk purchase recoverable is only the excess over the original contract price; if the risk purchase rate is lower, the excess is nil, so nothing is recoverable on that account.

q: Imprest stores held by a field official are produced for periodical verification. The official must account for the imprest by:

options.A: Producing only the cash equivalent of the stores originally issued
options.B: Returning all the stores to the depot before verification
options.C: Producing the stores on hand together with the account of stores consumed on works, so that the total imprest is accounted for
options.D: Obtaining a certificate from the supplier of the stores

e: An imprest holder accounts for the full imprest by producing stores on hand plus vouchers for stores consumed on works; the two together must equal the imprest quantity issued to him.

q: A workshop draws stores from a depot for a manufacturing job and, on completion of the job, is left with surplus material. The surplus material, when returned to the depot and taken into stock, is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting the job/workshop manufacturing account, so that the job is not overcharged with the cost of material not consumed on it
options.B: Debiting the Stock Adjustment Account as a loss
options.C: Crediting the Sales Suspense Account as a sale
options.D: Making no entry, as the material was already charged once

e: Surplus material returned by a workshop on completion of a job is taken into stock with credit to the job or manufacturing account, so the job bears only the cost of material actually consumed on it.

q: In the internal check of stores transactions, it is noticed that a purchase order was placed without the indent having been vetted by Finance where such vetting was required. The omission is:

options.A: A matter of no consequence, as vetting is optional in all cases
options.B: To be regularised by the depot storekeeper on his own authority
options.C: Decided by the supplier of the stores
options.D: An irregularity to be brought out by the Accounts office for regularisation under the orders of the competent authority

e: Placing a purchase order without required Finance vetting of the indent is an irregularity; Accounts must bring it out for regularisation under orders of the competent authority, and vetting is not optional.

q: Before covering a demand for a stock item, the purchase office searches the material management system (iMMS) and finds adequate stock of the same PL item lying in another depot. The correct action is to:

options.A: Ignore the stock and place a fresh purchase order in all cases
options.B: Arrange transfer of the available stock from the other depot, avoiding a fresh purchase to that extent
options.C: Declare the stock in the other depot as dead surplus
options.D: Ask the demanding department to cancel its demand

e: If iMMS shows adequate stock of the same PL item in another depot, that stock is transferred to meet the demand instead of placing a fresh purchase, avoiding unnecessary procurement and excess stock.

q: In a periodical review of non-moving and slow-moving stores, an item classified as 'S' (slow-moving) in FSN analysis is primarily examined to decide whether:

options.A: It should be condemned as scrap forthwith
options.B: Its book rate should be enhanced
options.C: The stock held is in excess of foreseeable requirements and should be declared surplus for circulation or disposal
options.D: It should be transferred to the Tools and Plant register

e: A slow-moving S item in FSN review is examined whether stock held exceeds foreseeable requirements, so excess can be declared surplus for circulation to other depots or for disposal.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores become obsolete when they are no longer usable for the purpose for which they were procured, e.g. due to a change in design or technology, even if they were issued recently.
2. Stores are surplus when, though serviceable and usable, they are held in excess of the requirements of the depot.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Obsolete stores are unusable for their original purpose due to design or technology change, while surplus stores are serviceable and usable but held in excess of requirements; both definitions are correct.

q: The average stock of stores held by a railway is reduced substantially through better inventory control, other things remaining the same. The annual inventory carrying cost borne by the railway will:

options.A: Increase in the same proportion
options.B: Remain unaffected, as carrying cost does not depend on stock held
options.C: Be transferred to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Decrease, as carrying cost is worked out as a percentage of the average value of stock held

e: Inventory carrying cost is calculated as a percentage of average value of stock held; reducing average stock, other things equal, directly reduces the annual carrying cost borne.

q:
Consider the following statements about emergency purchases of stores:
1. In an emergency, the normal tender procedure may be dispensed with by the competent authority for recorded reasons.
2. Even in an emergency purchase, the sanction of the competent authority and the reasonableness of the price paid are required.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In a genuine emergency the competent authority may dispense with normal tender procedure for recorded reasons, but sanction of the competent authority and reasonableness of price remain essential; both statements are correct.

q: A DS-8 issue note is distinguished from a transfer advice/note used between depots in that:

options.A: Both documents are used only for the sale of scrap
options.B: The transfer note is prepared by the supplier, while the issue note is prepared by the purchaser
options.C: An issue note authorises issue of stores from a depot to a consuming department or work, while a transfer note covers despatch of stores from one depot to another depot
options.D: An issue note is used only for imported stores

e: An issue note such as DS-8 authorises issue from a depot to a consuming department or work, while a transfer advice or note covers despatch between depots; the destination and accountal differ.

q: The stock of an item in a depot falls to its danger level. The immediate action expected of the depot and the purchase organisation is to:

options.A: Initiate urgent/emergency procurement action and expedite supplies, the danger level indicating that stock may be exhausted before normal replenishment arrives
options.B: Wait for the next annual review of stock levels
options.C: Declare the item as surplus to requirements
options.D: Stop all issues of the item permanently

e: Danger level means stock may exhaust before normal replenishment arrives, so urgent procurement and expediting are initiated at once rather than waiting for annual review or stopping issues.

q: Every stores item in the priced list bears a prescribed unit of account (e.g. each, kilogram, metre or litre) in its nomenclature. Issues of the item from the depot are made and priced:

options.A: In any unit convenient to the storekeeper
options.B: Only in the unit in which the supplier prefers to bill
options.C: Only in bulk lots fixed by the Tender Committee
options.D: In the prescribed unit of account of the item, so that the custody and priced accounts remain comparable

e: Issues are made and priced only in the prescribed unit of account in the item nomenclature - each, kg, metre or litre - so custody and priced accounts stay comparable and auditable.

q: An amount has remained outstanding under Stores Miscellaneous Suspense, representing a payment made by the Stores Accounts office on behalf of a department, pending raising of the debit. The balance is cleared by:

options.A: Writing it off as a loss after one month
options.B: Raising the debit against the department/head of account concerned and obtaining its acceptance, whereupon the suspense is relieved
options.C: Transferring it permanently to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Refunding the amount to the supplier

e: Stores Miscellaneous Suspense for a payment made on behalf of a department is cleared by raising the debit against the concerned department or head and obtaining its acceptance, relieving the suspense.

q: Material released from a completed work is returned to a depot in a mixed lot. On examination, part of it is found serviceable and part unserviceable. The correct treatment is that:

options.A: The entire lot is taken into priced stock as serviceable material
options.B: The entire lot is sold as scrap without examination
options.C: The serviceable portion is taken into stock and the unserviceable portion is segregated for survey and disposal as scrap
options.D: The entire lot is returned to the work site for disposal by the work officials

e: Mixed material released from a work is examined on return: the serviceable portion is taken into priced stock and the unserviceable portion is segregated for survey and disposal as scrap.

q: Copper and brass fittings held in a depot are stores which are 'attractive' in nature and prone to pilferage. In addition to their safe custody under lock and key, issues of such stores are made:

options.A: Only against properly authorised requisitions, with careful accountal of the quantities issued and returned
options.B: Freely to any department without a requisition, to save time
options.C: Only once a year, at the time of stock verification
options.D: Directly by the supplier to the consuming department

e: Attractive stores prone to pilferage, such as copper and brass fittings, are kept under lock and key and issued only against properly authorised requisitions, with careful accountal of issues and returns.

q: A stock sheet for a shortage is submitted for approval, and the stockholder represents that the shortage arose from a cause beyond his control. Before recovery is enforced, the representation is:

options.A: Ignored, recovery being automatic in every case of shortage
options.B: Decided by the stock verifier himself finally
options.C: Forwarded to the supplier for his orders
options.D: Considered by the competent authority while approving the stock sheet and deciding the responsibility for, and recovery or write-off of, the shortage

e: A stockholder representation that a shortage was beyond his control must be considered by the competent authority while approving the stock sheet and deciding responsibility, recovery or write-off; recovery is not automatic.

q: Stores which have been surveyed off and sold in an e-auction continue to stand in the stock accounts of the depot until:

options.A: The close of the financial year in which they are surveyed off
options.B: The sale is completed and delivery effected to the purchaser, whereupon the book value is adjusted, the difference between the sale value and the book value being taken to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: The next stock verification of the depot is held
options.D: The purchaser deposits the earnest money for the lot

e: Surveyed-off scrap remains in stock accounts until sale is completed and delivery effected; then the book value is removed and the difference between sale value and book value is taken to the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A depot of one zonal railway transfers a stores item to a depot of another zonal railway. The receiving depot holds the same item at a different book rate and proposes to take the transferred material into stock at its own rate. The correct position is that the transfer is priced at:

options.A: The current market rate of the item on the date of transfer
options.B: The book rate at which the receiving depot holds the item
options.C: The book rate of the issuing railway, the receiving depot taking the material into stock at that transfer value
options.D: An assessed value fixed jointly by the two depot officers

e: Inter-railway transfers are priced at the book rate of the issuing railway, and the receiving depot takes the material into stock at that transfer value, not at its own differing book rate or market rate.

q: Periodical (scheduled) indents for stock items are distinguished from special (non-scheduled) indents in that scheduled indents are:

options.A: Raised only after the stock of the item has been completely exhausted
options.B: Raised at prescribed intervals to maintain the coverage of stock items, while special indents are raised for urgent or unforeseen requirements arising outside the schedule
options.C: Placed directly on suppliers by the depot without reference to the purchase office
options.D: Used only for the procurement of imported stores

e: Scheduled indents are raised at prescribed intervals to maintain coverage of stock items, while special or non-scheduled indents meet urgent or unforeseen requirements arising outside the schedule.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Directorate General of Supplies and Disposals (DGS&D) continues to conclude rate contracts for common-user goods and services required by Government buyers.
2. Rate contracts for common-user goods and services, earlier concluded by DGS&D, are now available to Government buyers on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM).
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 2 only

e: DGS&D rate contracts for common-user goods and services have ceased; such procurement is now made through the Government e-Marketplace, GeM, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: During a major breakdown, a loco shed urgently requires a stores item which is not in stock in its depot, but a sister depot of the same railway holds adequate stock. The item is obtained from the sister depot on a 'loan' basis. This means that the borrowing depot:

options.A: Purchases the item permanently from the lending depot at the current market rate
options.B: Takes the item free of cost, no accountal of the loan being necessary
options.C: Sells the item back to the lending depot after use at the scrap rate
options.D: Must return the item to the lending depot in due course, or replace it, the loan not being a permanent transfer of the stores

e: Stores taken on loan from a sister depot are not a permanent transfer or free issue; the borrowing depot must return or replace the item in due course and the loan is properly accounted for.

q: A Survey Committee has examined certain unserviceable stores in a depot and recommended their condemnation, but the sanction of the competent authority to the condemnation and disposal has not yet been received. The correct course for the depot is to:

options.A: Keep the stores segregated in the depot and include them in an e-auction only after the condemnation and disposal are sanctioned by the competent authority
options.B: Include the stores in the next e-auction at once, sanction being a mere formality which can follow the sale
options.C: Issue the stores to a consuming department for use until sanction is received
options.D: Remove the stores from the stock accounts on the date of the Committee's recommendation itself

e: Survey Committee recommendation alone does not authorise sale; stores stay segregated and are included in e-auction only after condemnation and disposal are sanctioned by the competent authority.

q: Stores in a depot are physically issued on the first-in-first-out basis, the oldest lot being issued first. The value charged to the consuming department for such an issue is, however, worked out at:

options.A: The purchase rate of the oldest lot held in stock
options.B: The maximum retail price of the item
options.C: The purchase rate of the latest lot received in stock
options.D: The average (book) rate of the item current at the time of the issue

e: Physical issue follows first-in-first-out, but valuation follows the priced ledger system: issues are charged at the average book rate current at the time of issue, not at the rate of the oldest or latest lot.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where cent per cent inspection of every unit of a large lot of stores is impracticable, inspection may be carried out on a sampling basis in accordance with the prescribed sampling plan.
2. For stores or equipment which are under manufacture, inspection may be carried out in stages during the process of manufacture itself.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Where 100 percent inspection is impracticable, sampling inspection per the prescribed plan is permitted, and for items under manufacture stage inspection during manufacture is also provided for; both statements are correct.

q: Roller bearings released from rolling stock during periodical overhaul are returned by the workshop to the stores depot. Pending and after examination of the returned bearings, the correct treatment is that:

options.A: All the returned bearings are taken into priced stock as new bearings at the full book rate
options.B: All the returned bearings are sold as scrap without any examination
options.C: The bearings are issued back to the workshop without being taken into the depot accounts
options.D: The bearings are kept segregated under the custody of the stockholder; those found serviceable on examination are taken into stock, the workshop being given credit at the assessed value, and those found unserviceable are segregated for survey and disposal

e: Returned bearings are kept segregated in stockholder custody; serviceable ones on examination are taken into stock with credit to the workshop at assessed value, and unserviceable ones are segregated for survey and disposal.

q: A stock sheet for differences found in stock verification has been approved by the competent authority, who has ordered recovery for a part of the shortage and write-off of the balance. The stock sheet is treated as finally closed only when:

options.A: The stockholder signs the stock sheet in token of acceptance of the physical count
options.B: The next periodical verification of the depot is completed
options.C: The supplier of the item confirms the quantity originally supplied by him
options.D: The adjustment is passed through the Stock Adjustment Account in accordance with the orders on the sheet and the custody and priced records are corrected to agree with the physical balance

e: An approved stock sheet is finally closed only when the adjustment is passed through the Stock Adjustment Account as ordered - recovery and write-off as sanctioned - and custody and priced records are corrected to the physical balance.

q: In the internal check of a depot's priced accounts, the Stores Accounts office finds that a receipt of stores stands recorded in the priced stores ledger, but the corresponding receipt note has not been received from the depot. The discrepancy is cleared by:

options.A: Writing off the value of the receipt through the Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: Taking up the matter with the depot, obtaining the missing receipt note and linking it with the priced account, so that the receipt is fully supported by documents
options.C: Debiting the value of the receipt to the stockholder personally
options.D: Treating the receipt as a sale and crediting the amount to Sales Suspense

e: A receipt recorded in the priced stores ledger but not supported by a receipt note is cleared in internal check by taking up the matter with the depot, obtaining the missing receipt note and linking it with the priced account, so that the receipt stands fully supported by documents (Answer: B).

q: Stores are stolen from a depot and the custodian applies for the loss to be written off immediately so that the stock accounts can be squared up. The correct course is that the loss is written off:

options.A: By the stock verifier on the spot, on the date the theft is noticed
options.B: Only after the matter has been reported and enquired into, responsibility for the loss fixed, and the write-off sanctioned by the competent authority, the value being then adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: Automatically at the close of the financial year, without any enquiry
options.D: By the supplier who had supplied the stores, by free replacement of the stolen quantity

e: Stolen stores are written off only after report and enquiry, fixing of responsibility and sanction of the competent authority, the value then being adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account; immediate write-off is not permitted.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The force majeure clause in a stores contract relieves a party from liability for failure to perform the contract where the failure is due to events beyond its control, such as an act of God or war.
2. A mere rise in the market prices of stores is a force majeure event which relieves the supplier of his obligation to supply at the contracted rate.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Force majeure covers events beyond control such as act of God or war, relieving performance to that extent; a mere rise in market prices is not force majeure and does not relieve the supplier, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: In an e-auction of scrap, the highest bid received for a lot is below the reserve (upset) price fixed for that lot. The correct outcome is that:

options.A: The lot is knocked down to the highest bidder, the reserve price being only indicative
options.B: The earnest money of all the bidders for the lot is forfeited to the Railway
options.C: The depot officer accepts the bid and recovers the difference from the stockholder
options.D: The bid is not accepted as a concluded sale; the lot remains unsold and is re-offered in a subsequent auction after review of the reserve price by the competent authority

e: A highest bid below the reserve price is not a concluded sale; the lot remains unsold and is re-offered in a later auction after review of the reserve price by the competent authority.

q: A railway employee wishes to purchase, for his personal use, a serviceable stores item which has been declared surplus in a depot. The item can be sold to him only:

options.A: Free of cost, surplus stores being of no use to the Railway
options.B: At the book rate alone, departmental charges being not leviable on railway employees
options.C: With the sanction of the competent authority, at the book value plus the prescribed departmental charges, the amount being deposited before the item is delivered to him
options.D: Through an e-auction in which only railway employees are allowed to bid

e: A serviceable surplus item can be sold to a railway employee only with sanction of the competent authority at book value plus prescribed departmental charges, deposited before delivery.

q: A supplier has despatched stores against a purchase order and the bulk of the bill has been paid against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, but the material has not yet arrived at the consignee depot at the close of the financial year. In the stores accounts, the material is correctly treated as:

options.A: Stores in transit, represented under Purchase Suspense, and not as priced stock of the consignee depot until it is received, inspected and accepted there
options.B: Priced stock of the consignee depot from the date of despatch itself
options.C: A sale, the amount paid being transferred to Sales Suspense
options.D: A loss of stores, to be written off under competent sanction

e: Material paid for against despatch documents but not yet received at the consignee depot at year end is stores in transit under Purchase Suspense, not priced stock, until received, inspected and accepted there.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before an order banning business dealings with a firm is issued, the firm is ordinarily given an opportunity to show cause against the proposed action.
2. Orders banning or suspending business dealings with a firm are communicated to the other railways and units, so that the firm does not obtain orders elsewhere during the currency of the ban.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Banning business dealings requires prior show-cause opportunity to the firm in ordinary course, and ban or suspension orders are circulated to other railways and units to prevent orders elsewhere during the ban; both statements are correct.

q: An item of stores is required once only, for a specific sanctioned work, and has no regular consumption in the depot. The item is correctly procured as:

options.A: A stock item, by adding it to the priced vocabulary of the depot against its AAC
options.B: An imprest item, to be replenished periodically by the depot
options.C: A dead surplus item, after circulation to other depots
options.D: A non-stock item, against the specific demand of the work, its cost being charged direct to the work on receipt instead of being taken into depot stock

e: A one-time item for a specific sanctioned work with no regular consumption is a non-stock item, charged direct to the work on receipt, and not added to the depot priced vocabulary as a stock item against AAC.

q: A rate contract for an item has expired, but a consuming department places an indent for the item and the purchase office proposes to place a supply order on the erstwhile rate-contract firm at the old contracted rate. The correct position is that:

options.A: Supply orders can be placed at the old rate indefinitely, a rate contract once concluded remaining operative
options.B: The supply order is valid if the firm agrees to supply at the old rate, no fresh arrangement being needed
options.C: Supplies must be ordered during the currency of the rate contract; after its expiry, procurement has to be arranged afresh under a new contract or tender, and an order placed after expiry is not covered by the expired contract
options.D: The expired rate contract is automatically extended for one more year at the same rate

e: Supply orders under a rate contract can be placed only during its currency; after expiry procurement must be arranged afresh by a new contract or tender, and an order after expiry is not covered by the expired contract.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores supplied by a supplier in excess of the quantity ordered, beyond any tolerance permitted under the contract, need not be accepted by the consignee, and the excess may be returned to the supplier at his cost.
2. Stores supplied in excess of the ordered quantity must in all cases be accepted and paid for by the Railway, as the material has already been despatched.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Excess supply beyond the ordered quantity and any permitted tolerance need not be accepted and may be returned at the supplier cost; the Railway is not bound to accept and pay for all excess despatched, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A purchase order prescribes pre-despatch inspection of the stores by RITES as the inspecting agency. The supplier, without getting the material inspected, despatches it to the consignee depot and presents his bill. The correct course is that:

options.A: The material must be accepted into stock and the bill paid in full, inspection being the supplier's own concern
options.B: The material is not accepted into priced stock and payment is not passed as a matter of course; the case is regularised only in accordance with the contract, the prescribed inspection being got carried out or the lapse dealt with by the competent authority
options.C: The material is sold in an e-auction and the sale proceeds paid to the supplier
options.D: The consignee depot carries out the RITES inspection itself and issues the inspection certificate

e: Material despatched without the prescribed pre-despatch inspection by RITES is not accepted into priced stock or paid for as a matter of course; the lapse is regularised only as per contract by the competent authority after getting inspection done or dealing with the default.

q: For certain stores, the purchase order provides that acceptance will be based on the material test certificate furnished by the supplier. In such a case, the consignee depot accepts the stores when:

options.A: The supplier merely declares verbally that the material conforms to the specification
options.B: The material is accompanied by the prescribed test certificate of the manufacturer or an approved laboratory, and the consignee's own check of the quantity and condition of the material is satisfactory
options.C: The material has been paid for in advance against despatch documents
options.D: The material is accepted without any test certificate, the certificate being called for only if a defect appears later

e: Where acceptance is on a material test certificate, the depot accepts stores only when the prescribed manufacturer or approved laboratory test certificate accompanies the material and its own check of quantity and condition is satisfactory.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where a material change is made in the conditions of a stores tender after the tender notice has been issued, a verbal intimation to a few known tenderers is sufficient and no formal notice is necessary.
2. Such a change is brought to the notice of all concerned by a corrigendum to the tender notice, and the due date for submission of offers may be suitably extended so that tenderers can take the change into account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A material change in tender conditions after issue of the notice must be notified to all concerned by a formal corrigendum, with due date suitably extended if needed; verbal intimation to a few tenderers is insufficient, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Stores supplied against a contract are found defective a few months after their acceptance at the destination depot. The supplier disputes the warranty claim, contending that the warranty period, reckoned by him from the date of despatch of the stores, has expired. The correct position under the contract is that the warranty period ordinarily commences from:

options.A: The date of acceptance of the stores at the destination, so that a defect noticed within the warranty period so reckoned is covered by the warranty clause
options.B: The date of manufacture of the stores at the supplier's works
options.C: The date of issue of the stores from the depot to the consuming department
options.D: The date of payment of the supplier's bill

e: Warranty period under stores contracts is ordinarily reckoned from the date of acceptance of stores at destination, not from despatch, manufacture, issue or payment, so a defect noticed within that period is covered.

q: A supplier, apprehending delay, applies for extension of the delivery period before its expiry. The competent authority extends the delivery period, reserving the Railway's right to levy liquidated damages. Supplies made during the extended period are:

options.A: Liable to liquidated damages for the period of delay in accordance with the contract, the extension having been granted with that reservation
options.B: Deemed to have been made within the original delivery period, no liquidated damages being leviable for the extended portion
options.C: Paid for at a higher rate to compensate the supplier for the delay
options.D: Treated as supplies under a fresh contract at current market rates

e: Extension of delivery period granted reserving the right to levy liquidated damages leaves supplies in the extended period liable to liquidated damages for the delay as per contract, despite the extension.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 'stock-out' cost of a stores item is the loss or extra expense occasioned when the item is not available in stock at the time it is demanded.
2. A higher 'service level' for a stock item denotes that a higher proportion of the demands for the item is met from stock.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Stock-out cost is the loss or extra expense when an item is unavailable on demand, and a higher service level means a higher proportion of demands is met from stock; both statements are correct.

q: A value analysis study of a stores item finds that a cheaper standard material can perform the same function satisfactorily in place of the costlier material hitherto stocked. The substitution is correctly given effect to by:

options.A: The storekeeper on his own authority, by issuing the cheaper material against demands for the costlier item
options.B: The supplier, by supplying the cheaper material against the existing purchase order without any amendment
options.C: Adoption of the substitute material with the approval of the competent authority, the specification and stocking of the item being revised accordingly
options.D: Declaring the entire stock of the costlier material as scrap and selling it in an e-auction

e: A value analysis substitution is given effect only with approval of the competent authority and revision of specification and stocking accordingly; neither the storekeeper nor the supplier can substitute on their own.

q: A depot stocks bolts of the same description in several different sizes, each size being used for a distinct purpose. For correct identification and accounting, the correct codification is that:

options.A: Every distinct size of the item is allotted a separate PL number, a PL number identifying one distinct item of stores and no other
options.B: All sizes of the item are borne on a single PL number, the size being noted only on the bin card
options.C: A fresh PL number is allotted to the item each time fresh stock is received
options.D: The PL number of the item is changed at each depot according to local convenience

e: Each distinct item, including each distinct size of bolts, bears a separate PL number; one PL number identifies one distinct stores item only, ensuring correct identification, pricing and accounting.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Inflammable stores, such as petrol, oils and paints, are kept segregated in suitable storage away from general stores, as a precaution against fire.
2. 'Attractive' stores, such as copper and brass fittings, may be kept in open racks without lock and key, so that they can be issued quickly on demand.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Inflammable stores are segregated in suitable storage away from general stores as a fire precaution, but attractive stores cannot be kept in open unlocked racks; they need lock and key, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Against a purchase order, a supplier bills for the full quantity ordered, but the consignee depot has so far received and accepted only a part of the quantity. The supplier's bill is correctly passed for payment:

options.A: For the full quantity billed, the balance material being expected to arrive in due course
options.B: For no amount at all until the entire quantity ordered has been received
options.C: By the depot storekeeper directly, without reference to the receipt note
options.D: Only for the quantity actually received, inspected and accepted at the depot, the balance being paid when the remaining quantity is received and accepted

e: A supplier bill is passed only for the quantity actually received, inspected and accepted at the depot as per the receipt note; the balance is paid only when the remaining quantity is received and accepted.

q: An indenting department specifies a particular trade or brand name in its demand for a stores item. On the demand being taken up for procurement, the correct course is that:

options.A: The item must be purchased of the named brand in all cases, the department's preference being final
options.B: Specifications for procurement are required to be broad-based and generic, so as to obtain competition; procurement of a particular brand is resorted to only where the item is covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate or is otherwise justified and sanctioned
options.C: The demand is returned to the department without any procurement action in every such case
options.D: The tender is invited only from the manufacturer of the named brand and his dealers in all cases

e: Procurement specifications must be broad-based and generic to obtain competition under GFR; brand-specific procurement is allowed only where covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate or otherwise justified and sanctioned.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Demurrage charges for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for unloading a stores consignment at the destination depot are borne on the Railway's account where the unloading of the consignment is the depot's responsibility.
2. Such demurrage is recoverable from the supplier in every case, even where the consignment was booked on F.O.R. destination terms and the delay occurred in unloading at the destination.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Demurrage for detention beyond free time in unloading at destination, where unloading is the depot responsibility, is borne by the Railway; it is not recoverable from the supplier in every case, for example on F.O.R. destination terms, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A tenderer for stores attaches to his offer a condition varying the stipulated terms of delivery and payment in his favour. Such an offer is liable to be:

options.A: Accepted automatically at the rate quoted, the condition being ignored by the Railway
options.B: Treated as a conditional offer which does not conform to the tender conditions, and ignored or rejected in accordance with the tender conditions
options.C: Accepted only after the other tenderers agree to the same condition
options.D: Referred to the stock verifier for a decision on its acceptability

e: An offer imposing a condition varying stipulated delivery or payment terms is a conditional, non-conforming offer, liable to be ignored or rejected as per tender conditions, and cannot be accepted by simply ignoring the condition.

q: In a stores tender, the offers received show an identical pattern of rates, indicating that the tenderers have formed a cartel and quoted collusive rates. In such a case, the tender is liable to be:

options.A: Accepted in favour of the tenderer who submitted his offer first
options.B: Decided by drawing lots among the tenderers
options.C: Awarded to all the tenderers in equal shares at the quoted rates
options.D: Discharged by the competent authority and a fresh tender invited, the collusive quoting being dealt with as per the rules

e: Identical patterned rates indicating a cartel or collusive bidding are dealt with by discharging the tender and inviting a fresh tender, with action against collusive quoting as per rules; the tender is not awarded among the cartel.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Material received at a depot is taken into the priced stock accounts immediately on its arrival, before it has been inspected.
2. Material is taken into priced stock only after it has been inspected and accepted, a receipt note being prepared for the quantity accepted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Material is taken into priced stock only after inspection and acceptance, on the basis of a receipt note for the accepted quantity; mere arrival before inspection does not bring it into priced stock, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Supplies against a purchase order are heavily overdue and the supplier is not responding to reminders. The purchase office, in 'progressing' the order, is expected to:

options.A: Pursue the supplier actively for the outstanding supply, obtain a firm revised delivery commitment where justified, and, failing satisfactory supply, initiate action for extension, cancellation and risk purchase in accordance with the contract
options.B: Wait indefinitely for the supplies, progressing being confined to filing the correspondence
options.C: Cancel the AAC of the item so that the demand lapses
options.D: Direct the consignee depot to manufacture the item in the railway workshop in every case

e: Progressing an overdue order means actively pursuing the supplier, obtaining a firm revised commitment where justified, and failing satisfactory supply, initiating extension, cancellation and risk purchase action as per contract.

q: Against a purchase order, a substantial part of the quantity has been supplied and accepted, but the balance quantity is no longer required because the programme for which it was ordered has been curtailed. The purchase order is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Compelling the supplier to supply the balance quantity, which is then declared as dead surplus
options.B: Short-closing the order for the balance quantity with the consent of the supplier, so that the contract is closed without claims on either side for that quantity
options.C: Returning the quantity already supplied to the supplier for a full refund
options.D: Transferring the balance quantity to another supplier at the same rate without any formality

e: Where the balance quantity is no longer required due to curtailment of the programme, the order is short-closed for that balance with the supplier consent, closing the contract for that quantity without claims on either side.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Stores Budget of a railway is a primary budget, prepared independently of the estimates of works and the revenue programmes of the departments.
2. The 'deduct entry' in the Stores Budget is a minus entry which increases the total debits provided for stores during the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Stores Budget is not a primary independent budget - it is built on works estimates and departmental programmes - and the deduct entry is a minus entry that reduces, not increases, total stores debits; so neither statement is correct.

q: Stores in a depot are destroyed by a fire, and the enquiry ordered into the loss establishes that the custodian had taken all reasonable care and precautions and that no negligence attaches to him. The correct treatment of the loss is that:

options.A: The full value of the stores is recovered from the custodian in every case of loss, negligence or no negligence
options.B: The stores are replaced free of cost by the supplier who had supplied them
options.C: The custodian is not held personally liable for the loss, which is written off under the sanction of the competent authority and adjusted in the stores accounts
options.D: The loss is adjusted by reducing the book rates of the remaining stock of the item

e: Where enquiry establishes the custodian took all reasonable care and no negligence attaches in a fire loss, he is not personally liable; the loss is written off under competent sanction and adjusted in the stores accounts.

q: A supplier has completed the supplies against a contract satisfactorily and applies for refund of his Security Deposit immediately on despatch of the first consignment. The Security Deposit is correctly refunded:

options.A: Only after satisfactory completion of the contract and fulfilment of the obligations secured by the deposit, in accordance with the contract conditions
options.B: On despatch of the first consignment itself, the balance supplies being unsecured
options.C: Only after the stores supplied are consumed by the using departments
options.D: Only at the close of the financial year following the year of the contract

e: Security Deposit is refunded only after satisfactory completion of the contract and fulfilment of all obligations it secures, as per contract conditions, not on despatch of the first consignment.

q: Amounts are found due to the Railway from a supplier under a stores contract, but nothing remains payable to him under that contract from which the dues can be recovered. In such a case, the dues may be recovered from:

options.A: The earnest money deposited by the other tenderers in the same tender
options.B: Amounts payable to the supplier under his other contracts with the Railway, or from his security held by the Railway, in accordance with the contract conditions
options.C: The pay of the depot stockholder who received the stores
options.D: The sale proceeds of the next e-auction of scrap

e: Dues from a supplier with nothing payable under that contract may be recovered from amounts payable to him under other contracts with the Railway or from his security held, as per contract conditions.

q: A tenderer withdraws his offer for stores during the period of validity of the tender, without the consent of the Railway. The consequence under the tender conditions is ordinarily that:

options.A: He is paid compensation for the expenses incurred in preparing the tender
options.B: His offer is kept alive by the Railway until the tender is decided
options.C: He is awarded the contract at the rate quoted by the next higher tenderer
options.D: His Earnest Money Deposit is liable to be forfeited

e: Withdrawal of an offer during its validity without Railway consent makes the tenderer liable to forfeiture of his Earnest Money Deposit under the tender conditions.

q: A newly registered firm, which has not so far supplied a particular stores item to the Railways, offers competitive rates for a large requirement of the item. Before a bulk order is placed on the firm, the prudent course ordinarily adopted is to:

options.A: Place the entire bulk order on the firm at once, its registration being a guarantee of performance
options.B: Debar the firm from the tender as it has no past performance
options.C: Place a small 'trial' (developmental) order on the firm, so that its capability and the quality of its supplies are proved before bulk orders are entrusted to it
options.D: Require the firm to supply the entire quantity free of cost as a sample

e: For an unproved newly registered firm, a small trial or developmental order is placed first to prove its capability and supply quality before entrusting bulk orders; registration alone is not a guarantee of performance.

q: A common-use item of stores is available on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), but a department proposes to procure it from outside GeM on the ground of convenience. Before such outside procurement is resorted to, the buyer is required to:

options.A: Generate the prescribed availability report/certificate on GeM recording that the item is not available on GeM, or is available only on the terms recorded therein
options.B: Obtain a Proprietary Article Certificate for the item in every case
options.C: Sell an equivalent quantity of surplus stores through e-auction
options.D: Obtain the sanction of the stock verifier for bypassing the portal

e: Procurement outside GeM for an item available on GeM requires the prescribed GeM Availability Report and Past Transaction Summary certificate recording non-availability or the terms on GeM, as per GFR and GeM rules.

q: A consuming department requires an item which is not held in stock in the depot serving it. The correct course of procurement is that:

options.A: The department places a purchase order directly on a supplier of its choice
options.B: The depot issues a transfer note to the supplier for the quantity required
options.C: The department sends its demand to the stores depot, and the depot, not holding the item in stock, raises an indent on the purchase office for arranging the procurement
options.D: The department borrows the item from a contractor executing works for the Railway

e: A department needing a non-stock item sends its demand to the stores depot, and the depot, not holding it, raises an indent on the purchase office to arrange procurement; the department does not order directly on a supplier.

q: A workshop has a heavy programme of periodical overhaul of rolling stock during the year, requiring large quantities of maintenance stores. To ensure that the stores are available when the programmed outturn falls due, the demands for such stores are:

options.A: Raised by the workshop as emergency demands on the day each vehicle is taken up for overhaul
options.B: Projected and consolidated in advance, linked to the overhaul programme, so that the depot and the purchase office can plan the coverage and procurement of the items in time
options.C: Met entirely from the dead surplus held in the depots of other railways
options.D: Placed by the workshop directly on suppliers through single tenders throughout the year

e: Stores for a programmed overhaul programme are projected and consolidated in advance linked to that programme, so the depot and purchase office can plan coverage and procurement in time, not raised as day-to-day emergencies.

q: The same PL item is held in two different wards of one stores depot, each ward being in the custody of a different storekeeper. For accounting purposes:

options.A: A separate priced ledger folio is maintained for each ward for the item
options.B: Separate bin cards are maintained in each ward for the quantities held there, but a single priced ledger folio is maintained for the item for the depot as a whole
options.C: No bin card is maintained, the priced ledger alone being sufficient for both wards
options.D: The item is treated as two distinct stores items with two PL numbers

e: Where the same PL item is held in two wards, separate bin cards are kept ward-wise for custody quantities, but a single priced ledger folio is maintained for the item for the depot as a whole.

q: On agreement of a depot's records, the quantities in the bin cards tally with the priced stores ledger, but the value in the priced ledger is found wrong because an incorrect rate was posted for a receipt. The correct rectification is that:

options.A: The value difference, being a price difference and not a quantity difference, is corrected in the priced accounts through the Stock Adjustment Account, the bin card quantities remaining untouched
options.B: The shortage is recovered in cash from the ward storekeeper
options.C: The bin card quantities are altered to match the wrong value
options.D: The receipt is deleted from the priced ledger altogether

e: A wrong rate posted for a receipt causes only a value difference, quantities tallying; it is corrected in the priced accounts through the Stock Adjustment Account, leaving bin card quantities untouched.

q:
Consider the following statements about issue notes:
1. Stores are issued from a depot against a duly authorised issue note/requisition, and the consuming department acknowledges receipt of the stores on the issue note.
2. Where the receipted copy of an issue note is not returned by the consuming department, the depot and the Accounts office follow up the case so that the issue is duly acknowledged and accounted for.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Issues are made only against a duly authorised issue note or requisition with acknowledgement by the consuming department, and unreturned receipted copies are followed up by the depot and Accounts; both statements are correct.

q: Stores are transferred from one depot to another depot of the same railway under a transfer note. The transfer is completed in the records when:

options.A: The material is loaded at the despatching depot
options.B: The material is consumed by the department attached to the receiving depot
options.C: The purchase office issues a fresh purchase order in favour of the receiving depot
options.D: The receiving depot receives the material, acknowledges it on the transfer document and takes it into its stock, whereupon the despatching depot relieves its stock

e: An inter-depot transfer is completed when the receiving depot receives the material, acknowledges it on the transfer document and takes it into stock, whereupon the despatching depot relieves its stock accordingly.

q: At night, a running shed urgently needs a small stores item held in the imprest of a field official to attend to a locomotive failure. The item is issued from the imprest at once. The issue is regularised by:

options.A: Treating the item as consumed without any record, the issue being at night
options.B: Selling the item to the shed and recovering cash on the spot
options.C: Returning an equivalent item to the imprest by the supplier
options.D: Recording the issue in the imprest account at once and accounting for the consumption in the normal imprest account rendered by the holder, so that the imprest is made good in due course

e: An urgent night issue from imprest is recorded at once in the imprest account and its consumption is accounted for in the normal imprest account rendered by the holder, so the imprest is made good in due course.

q: Stores are issued to a contractor on loan for use on a railway work being executed by him. Such loaned stores:

options.A: Become the property of the contractor on issue
options.B: Remain the property of the Railway, are to be used only on the railway work, and are to be returned to stores or duly accounted for on completion of the work
options.C: Are written off from the books on the date of issue in all cases
options.D: Are treated as scrap released from the work

e: Stores loaned to a contractor for a railway work remain Railway property, must be used only on that work, and must be returned to stores or duly accounted for on completion of the work.

q:
Consider the following statements about stores maintained specially for accident relief trains:
1. Such stores are held to a prescribed scale and kept ready for immediate use in an emergency.
2. Stores used from the relief train are replenished promptly, so that the relief train is not left short of its prescribed equipment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Accident relief train stores are held to a prescribed scale ready for immediate emergency use, and any stores used are replenished promptly to restore the full scale; both statements are correct.

q: High Speed Diesel stocked at a Railway Consumer Depot is accounted for as stores in that:

options.A: Receipts are taken into stock and issues to locomotives are recorded by measured quantity, the stock on hand being verifiable by measurement of the quantity in the tanks
options.B: It is issued free of accountal, being a running expense only
options.C: It is borne on the Tools and Plant register of the depot
options.D: It is accounted for only at the close of the financial year by a lump-sum entry

e: High Speed Diesel at a Railway Consumer Depot is accounted as stores by measured quantity - receipts into stock, issues to locomotives recorded, and stock on hand verifiable by tank measurement.

q: Uniform and clothing stores held in a depot are issued to railway staff:

options.A: To any employee on a verbal request, without reference to entitlement
options.B: As scrap, after the uniform has been stitched
options.C: Against the prescribed scale and entitlement of the staff concerned, the issues being recorded against the individuals/departments entitled to receive them
options.D: Only against cash payment by the staff in all cases

e: Uniform and clothing stores are issued only against the prescribed scale and entitlement of the staff concerned, with issues recorded against the entitled individuals or departments, not on verbal request.

q: Printed forms and stationery stores held in a depot include accountable forms such as receipt and issue note books. Such accountable forms are:

options.A: Issued freely to any department without any record of the serial numbers issued
options.B: Treated as ordinary waste paper after printing
options.C: Sold to staff for personal use at the book rate
options.D: Kept in safe custody and issued under proper accountal, so that their use can be traced and misuse prevented

e: Accountable printed forms such as receipt and issue note books are kept in safe custody and issued under proper accountal of serial numbers, so their use can be traced and misuse prevented.

q: Medicines held as medical stores have passed their expiry date while lying in stock. Such expired medicines are:

options.A: Issued on priority to patients before any fresh stock is used
options.B: Not issued for use, and are dealt with as unserviceable stores to be surveyed off and disposed of as per the prescribed procedure
options.C: Returned to the general stores depot for issue to workshops
options.D: Re-dated by the stockholder and retained in stock

e: Expired medicines are not issued for use; they are treated as unserviceable stores and surveyed off and disposed of under the prescribed procedure, and cannot be re-dated and retained.

q: A depot holds a mixed arising of scrap consisting of steel rails and copper cable. To obtain proper realisation in disposal, the scrap is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Segregating the ferrous scrap and the non-ferrous scrap into separate lots of like description before offering them for sale
options.B: Mixing the two together in a single lot so that the purchaser gets an average quality
options.C: Issuing the copper cable to workshops as serviceable stores without examination
options.D: Burying the non-ferrous scrap and selling only the ferrous scrap

e: Mixed scrap is segregated into separate lots of like description - ferrous and non-ferrous separately - before sale, so each lot fetches its proper realisation in e-auction.

q: A complete assembled unit released from service can be sold as scrap in a better condition as an assembled lot than if it is broken up into pieces. In forming lots for auction, an assembled lot means that:

options.A: Stores of all descriptions in the depot are assembled into one single lot
options.B: The lot is assembled by the purchaser after delivery at his own premises
options.C: The unit is offered and sold as one lot in its assembled condition, instead of being dismantled and sold piecemeal
options.D: Serviceable stock items are assembled with scrap to make up the lot weight

e: An assembled lot means a complete unit is offered and sold as one lot in its assembled condition instead of being dismantled and sold piecemeal, often fetching better realisation as a unit.

q: After delivery of scrap lots sold in an auction is completed, the depot renders a sale account so that the Accounts office can finally adjust the sale. The sale account primarily enables the Accounts office to:

options.A: Fix the reserve price for the next auction
options.B: Verify the physical stock of serviceable stores in the wards
options.C: Place a fresh purchase order for the quantity sold
options.D: Link the sale value realised for each lot with its delivery and adjust the difference between the sale value and the book value to the Stock Adjustment Account, clearing the amount held under Sales Suspense

e: The sale account enables Accounts to link sale value realised for each lot with its delivery, adjust the difference between sale value and book value to the Stock Adjustment Account, and clear the Sales Suspense balance.

q: A lot of scrap is put up in an e-auction but no bid at all is received for it. The correct disposal of the lot is that it:

options.A: Is delivered free of cost to the bidder of another lot
options.B: Is knocked down at the book value to the depot storekeeper
options.C: Is destroyed at the depot immediately after the auction
options.D: Remains unsold and is re-offered in a subsequent auction, if necessary after review of the lot and its reserve price by the competent authority

e: A lot receiving no bid remains unsold; it is re-offered in a subsequent auction, if necessary after review of the lot and its reserve price by the competent authority, and is not given away or destroyed.
